name: ULTRA-LOW TEMPERATURE -86°C
desc: Premium Vertical Ultra-Low Temperature (ULT) Laboratory Deep Freezer engineered for long-term preservation of critical bio-samples at temperatures down to -86°C. Features a massive 1000-liter SS internal cabinet, heavy-duty cascade refrigeration system, and integrated CO₂ backup system.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS ULTRA-LOW TEMPERATURE -86°C Deep Freezer is a premium vertical ultra-low temperature preservation system engineered for long-term storage of critical biological specimens, certified ATCC microbial cultures, vaccines, plasma derivatives, DNA/RNA libraries, enzymes, monoclonal antibodies, and temperature-sensitive pharmaceuticals at adjustable setpoints down to -86°C. Leveraging a heavy-duty cascade refrigeration architecture with dual compressors and eco-friendly CFC-free/HCFC-free refrigerants, the unit maintains micro-increment 1°C PID stability, while the integrated CO₂ backup system and chart recorder ensure continuous cold-chain integrity during power or compressor failure. Doctors rely on this freezer for storing mRNA vaccines, tissue biopsies, and blood components; B.Sc/M.Sc students use it to preserve microbial glycerol stocks (e.g., Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, Saccharomyces cerevisiae) and mammalian cell lines (e.g., HeLa, CHO, HEK293) in cryoprotectant media containing DMSO; PhD researchers and chemists store heat-labile reagents, RT-PCR master mixes, TRIzol-lysed RNA samples, sealed volatile organic solvents (e.g., isopropanol, ethanol) in secondary containment, and reference standards in compliance with ISO 20387 biobanking, CDC vaccine storage guidelines, and ASTM E1564 low-temperature storage practices, thereby safeguarding sample viability and experimental reproducibility.
sop: Ensure the deep freezer is connected to a dedicated 5KVA servo stabilizer and the power indicator is on; allow the unit to stabilize at the previously set temperature for at least 30 minutes before opening.
Visually inspect the outer door gasket, vacuum release port, and CO₂ backup cylinder pressure gauge; confirm the chart recorder paper/ink is sufficient for audit logging.
Unlock the outer door using the ergonomic handle and wait 5–10 seconds for the vacuum release port to equalize pressure before fully opening.
Press the 'SET' button once on the microprocessor PID controller; the setpoint value will flash on the high-visibility digital display.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., -80°C); each press changes the value in 1°C steps.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value; the controller will display the current internal chamber temperature and begin cooling/heating to the new setpoint.
Open only the specific insulated sub-door for the compartment you need, minimizing heat ingress; place pre-chilled sample racks or cryoboxes inside quickly and close the sub-door firmly.
Record the sample details (name, date, rack position, operator initials) in the logbook, and verify the temperature display returns to the setpoint within the specified recovery time.
Before closing the outer door, confirm no obstruction at the gasket, close the door, and engage the lock; activate the password security lock if configured.
Periodically test the audible/visible alarms by simulating a high-temperature condition or pressing the alarm test button, and confirm the CO₂ backup system activates.

Safety Warning: Always wear cryogenic gloves and face shield when handling ultra-low-temperature contents; never store non-sealed strong acids, explosive peroxides, or live cultures without proper secondary containment, and immediately vent the chamber after opening to avoid oxygen deficiency or CO₂ accumulation from the backup system.
